question: If a chord of a circle subtends an angle of 60circ at the circumference of the circle, then what is the ratio of the radius of the circle and the length of the chord respectively?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Using the Extended Sine Rule for a circle: Chord Length = 2 × Radius × sin(θ) Where θ is the angle subtended by the chord at the circumference. Length of chord = 2 × r × sin(60°) = 2 × r × (√3 ÷ 2) = r√3 Required Ratio = Radius : Chord = r : r√3 = 1 : √3 **∴ The correct answer is 1 : √3.**
